hook.passage: In May 2016, a public radio reporter in North Carolina sat down with a 17-year-old named Hunter Schafer and her parents. Weeks earlier, Schafer had become the youngest plaintiff in the ACLU's lawsuit against House Bill 2, the state law that made it illegal for her to use the women's bathroom in a public building. Asked whether it felt validating when strangers assumed she was a cisgender girl, she said it used to. Now that she was "exploring the nonbinary part of myself," it was different.
